events.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
events.description: After a voyage across the Atlantic Ocean from Spain, Christopher Columbus and his crew sighted and landed on an island in the Bahamas, which the native Lucayan people called Guanahani and Columbus named San Salvador.
events.significance: This landing began sustained contact between Europe and the Americas, ushering in an era of colonization, the Columbian Exchange, and profound demographic, cultural, and economic transformations worldwide.

events.title: Death of Robert E. Lee
events.description: Confederate General Robert E. Lee died in Lexington, Virginia, at age 63, five years after the end of the American Civil War, while serving as president of Washington College (later Washington and Lee University).
events.significance: Lee remains one of the most studied and debated figures in American history; his postwar advocacy for reconciliation and his legacy as a Confederate commander continue to shape discussions of memory and the Civil War.

events.title: Execution of Edith Cavell
events.description: British nurse Edith Cavell was executed by a German firing squad in Brussels for helping about 200 Allied soldiers escape German-occupied Belgium during World War I.
events.significance: Her execution caused international outrage, became a powerful propaganda tool for the Allies, and cemented her legacy as a symbol of humanitarian courage and patriotic self-sacrifice.

events.title: Khrushchev's Shoe Incident at the UN
events.description: Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev reportedly banged his shoe on the desk during a United Nations General Assembly session in New York, protesting a speech by Filipino delegate Lorenzo Sumulong about Soviet domination of Eastern Europe.
events.significance: The incident became an enduring image of Cold War tensions and the confrontational diplomacy between the Soviet Union and the West.

events.title: USS Cole Bombing
events.description: The guided-missile destroyer USS Cole was attacked by al-Qaeda suicide bombers in a small boat while refueling in the port of Aden, Yemen, killing 17 American sailors and injuring dozens more.
events.significance: The attack was one of the deadliest on a U.S. Navy vessel since the Vietnam War and was a precursor to the September 11, 2001 attacks, highlighting the growing threat of al-Qaeda.
